keywords: Verification process 2.Problem-solving process 3.Basic skills 4.Data handling skills 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: In this course, we will take up the characteristic objects and phenomena of the department to which each student belongs, and learn the basic skills required for the verification process and problem-solving process. Through experimental activities, learn the basics of "data handling skills" required to collect data → organize → analyze → hypothesis → visualization → report. In addition, students will learn the basic skills of "PBL for science and technology", including the process from problem finding to solution and the basic elements of verification activities. In the first half of "Data Handling Skills", students will investigate the attractiveness and issues of Nonoichi City through desktop research and fieldwork, summarize them on a handwritten map, and make poster presentations. In the second half of "PBL for science and technology" basic skill learning, students will plan and create original gamification teaching materials to make Nonoichi City aware of its attractions and issues, and will experience the PDCA cycle by repeating improvement activities. Finally, students will hold a final presentation of the attractions and issues of Nonoichi City and a hands-on experience of original gamification teaching materials.
requiredKnowledge: No textbook is specified, but necessary pre-survey and post-review are required for each lesson. In addition, since group activities outside of class hours are essential, each student is required to actively participate in group activities.
